title: Bitcoin’s Bottom Is Not a Matter of Belief
dek: Eight market narratives converge on a tempting conclusion. The evidence for distress is stronger than the evidence for a durable reversal.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a weathered copper Bitcoin medallion balanced on a fractured stone ledge above a shadowed chasm, with another ledge below; a metaphor for an uncertain market bottom.

title: Crypto’s rebound has a participation problem
dek: A brief improvement in market breadth does not erase persistent ETF withdrawals or a defensive technical structure.
image_alt: A copper pillar engraved with the Bitcoin symbol rises among descending dark stone columns, illustrating a narrow market rebound.

title: Crypto’s Narrow Rebound: Why Relative Strength Is Not a Recovery
dek: A market with only six advancing assets out of a hundred, persistent ETF redemptions and rising derivatives turnover deserves a harder test than a bounce in Bitcoin.
image_alt: Abstract editorial illustration of broad slate-colored channels converging on a narrow amber opening, representing a market rebound with limited participation.

title: Crypto’s Rebound Has a Conviction Problem
dek: Bitcoin is climbing off a bruising November low, and selected altcoins are showing life. But institutional withdrawals, weak Ethereum leadership and conflicting liquidity signals complicate the story behind the bounce.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a fractured market bridge whose two sections are beginning to reconnect, against a restrained dark grid

title: MINELIUS and the Wallet-Cluster Claim That Outran Its Evidence
dek: A Solana launch drew a startling bundled-buy warning. Conflicting scanner verdicts show why purchase patterns, holder balances and beneficial ownership must not be mistaken for one another.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial photograph of unlabeled brass discs connected by threads beneath a magnifying glass; an illustration of questions about wallet links, not a map of actual token holders.

title: The Wallet Is Large. The Owner Is Still a Question.
dek: A historical exchange wallet disclosure and a custodian’s own terms expose the mistake behind crypto rich lists: an address may show where assets sit, without revealing whose economic claims they satisfy.
image_alt: Conceptual illustration of one brass vault controlling access to several separate, blank claim certificates, representing the difference between custody and economic ownership; not a blockchain chart.

title: On-Chain Forensics Can Trace the Money. It Cannot Automatically Name the Owner.
dek: The Euler Finance recovery shows where blockchain evidence is strongest: transaction paths are verifiable, wallet clusters are inferential, and real-world attribution needs evidence the ledger does not contain.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial illustration of bronze wallet nodes linked by solid transaction arrows that fade into dashed paths toward unidentified silhouettes, representing the boundary between observable fund movement and uncertain human attribution; not a market chart.

title: Bitcoin ETF Flows Aren’t Bitcoin Buy Orders: How Creations and Redemptions Work
dek: Issuer filings separate net share creation, custodied BTC and changes in fund value—and the SEC’s in-kind rule change makes that distinction more important.
image_alt: Conceptual still life of ETF share certificates and a Bitcoin custody vault linked by opposing brass arrows, symbolizing cash or in-kind creation and redemption; not a market chart.

title: Token Unlocks: Why a Cliff Is Not the Same Supply Shock as Linear Vesting
dek: Arbitrum's original vesting disclosures put more than 1.1 billion insider tokens on a single modeled cliff, while a separate Foundation allocation accrued continuously. The timing difference is measurable; the selling pressure is not.
image_alt: Conceptual illustration of a stack of gold tokens behind a stone threshold beside a measured sequence of gold tokens on a pale ramp; not a market chart.

title: Tokenomics Fundamentals: Why Circulating, Total and Max Supply Tell Different Stories
dek: A UNI supply audit finds 623.3 million tokens classified as circulating, a disputed total, and a one-billion-token ceiling that is not necessarily permanent.
image_alt: Conceptual still life of three nested brass rings holding stone tokens beside a key, ledger and exposed mechanism, representing different supply classifications and governance authority; not market data.

title: Crypto Liquidity Basics: Why Daily Trading Volume Is Not the Liquidity You Can Sell Into
dek: A real pair of spot order books reveals what turnover totals leave out: available bids, available asks, and the price of crossing them for a specified trade size.
image_alt: Conceptual still life of a heavily marked brass counting drum over two stone water basins linked by a narrow sluice, illustrating how repeated trading activity differs from liquidity available at one moment; not market data.

title: Bitcoin Rebounded at $55,130. The Tape Still Won’t Name the Buyer.
dek: Binance and OKX show Bitcoin recovering while aggressive sellers remained in control of volume. The evidence supports absorption at the low—but not the identity or staying power of the buyers.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork of a massive cracked dark stone slab resting on a hidden bronze support beam, evoking unseen liquidity holding up a stressed market; not a market chart.

title: Bitcoin’s September High Met November’s ETF Exodus
dek: From $86,603 to $60,094 in 62 days, Bitcoin’s collapse exposed a harder question: did leveraged selling clear the market, or did spot demand retreat with it?
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a copper-and-stone financial bridge fracturing into a dark chasm, with copper panels falling away; a metaphor for Bitcoin’s failed rally and reversal in ETF demand, not a price chart.

title: DACITY: The Contract Was Not the Whole Risk
dek: A token can have reassuring permissions, apparently protected liquidity and a functioning sell market—and still leave the hardest questions about its launch unanswered.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork of a divided stone ledger suspended over disconnected paths, illustrating the gap between token contract safeguards and hidden ownership risk; not a market chart.

title: The Market Broke on Friday. Crypto’s Next Test Is Whether Liquidity Breaks With It.
dek: After a sharp U.S. equity selloff and a surge in expected volatility, the decisive question for digital assets is not whether fear spreads, but how funding, leverage and market depth respond.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork of two fractured dark market structures separated by a gap, with broken copper spans suggesting uncertain transmission of financial stress; not a market chart.

title: Bitcoin’s Bottom Is Not a Price. It Is a Change in Market Behavior.
dek: With Bitcoin testing its June low, the distinction between capitulation and genuine demand recovery matters more than any calendar prediction.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a weathered copper Bitcoin disk wedged between fractured layers of dark slate, symbolizing resilience under selling pressure.

title: When Losing Less Becomes a Trading Trap
dek: TRON held up better than Bitcoin during a violent crypto selloff, but a closer look at venue liquidity complicates the defensive narrative.
image_alt: A green rocky island above a stormy sea with its cracked, crumbling foundation visible below the waterline and red market candlesticks in the clouds

title: Bitcoin’s Bearish Trap: Weakness Is Not a Short Signal
dek: Six days of falling prices, renewed ETF withdrawals and aggressive derivatives selling tell a bearish story. The harder question is whether that story offers a viable trade.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a weathered copper Bitcoin disk on fractured descending slate beside a balance holding a feather, symbolizing conflicting market forces.

title: Zcash’s Momentum Test Turned on a Single Trade
dek: A November 18 screen of ten liquid crypto pairs found relative strength inside a broad selloff. A historical simulation exposed why none qualified for a trade.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial illustration of a precarious slate beam supported by one copper pillar, with detached blocks below, symbolizing a profitable historical result dependent on one exceptional trade; not a price chart.

title: Crypto’s Missing Edge: When Evidence Stops Short
dek: Bitcoin and Ethereum showed stress, liquidity and violent positioning shifts. But a convincing market story is not the same as a tested trading advantage.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork contrasting fractured market layers with a precision balance and blank research paper, symbolizing the gap between market narratives and tested evidence.

title: Crypto’s Fear Reading Is Extreme. The Market’s Weakness Runs Deeper.
dek: A November 16 snapshot shows widespread losses, shrinking derivatives exposure and a Bitcoin market still below its trend. The case for a bottom remains incomplete.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork of fractured dark market layers divided by a copper fault, beside a restrained balance symbol; not a factual price chart.

title: Bitcoin’s $62,000 Reversal Was Real. A Bottom Is Still Unproven.
dek: The November selloff triggered a cross-venue liquidation reversal. The missing piece is not another fear indicator—it is evidence that ordinary buyers can hold the line.
image_alt: Abstract editorial illustration of dark fractured horizontal layers beside a copper-colored rising line and circular marks.

title: INJ’s 95% Bridge Wallet Is Not the Whale Story It Appears to Be
dek: The Ethereum balance is real. The conclusion often attached to it is wrong. Injective’s harder questions concern cross-chain claims, native issuance and what “circulating supply” actually measures.
image_alt: Conceptual cutaway of a guarded vault filled with archival plates, with a smaller group of plates outside along a narrow bridge, illustrating custody versus circulating claims.

title: Bitcoin’s Rebound Was Real. The Trading Edge Was Unproven.
dek: A market can change direction before the evidence becomes strong enough to justify a trade.
image_alt: Conceptual illustration of a Bitcoin-marked disc on one balance pan, an empty opposite pan, and an hourglass behind them.

title: Bitcoin’s Four-Year Cycle Meets a Different Kind of Selloff
dek: The halving clock still fits the timing. ETF redemptions, higher real yields and unfinished crypto legislation may change what happens after the first liquidation.
image_alt: An abstract institutional stone facade fractured beside layered market bands and a restrained Bitcoin emblem, representing sudden shocks and prolonged selling.

title: Bitcoin’s Selling Chain: ETF Redemptions, Basis Unwinds and Treasury Debt
dek: ETF money is leaving just as leveraged hedges shrink and corporate Bitcoin balance sheets face a harder funding market. The evidence points to a transmission system—not one identifiable seller.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of three slate balance-sheet panels labeled ETF flows, CME hedges and BTC treasury connected by a strained copper line; conceptual artwork, not a market chart.

title: QUID, EDGE and KOR: When Product Success Fails to Reach the Token
dek: A useful product can attract customers without creating a valuable token. Three new launches expose the difference.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial design showing QUID, EDGE and KOR as three labeled circles above separate baselines, representing their distinct token-value-capture questions.

title: Bitcoin Fell While Open Interest Rose. That Complicates the Liquidation Story.
dek: A 29-day Hyperliquid record shows nearly $727 million in long liquidations alongside rising BTC-denominated open interest. The selloff was real; its dominant cause remains unsettled.
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork of opposing slate and copper pressure fields converging around a central circular fracture, representing competing explanations for Bitcoin selling.

title: Circle’s ARC Revenue Changed the Growth Story. The Valuation Question Is Harder.
dek: A $181.8 million token presale turned a contracting quarter into headline growth. What the filings, valuation arithmetic, and Arc blockchain evidence actually show.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a financial ledger with a separate amber ARC revenue layer, emphasizing the distinction between recurring earnings and token presale income.

title: Allora’s Insider Unlock: Why the Vesting Clock Is Not a Sell Order
dek: A 160-million-token cliff, conflicting supply classifications, and thin spot liquidity expose the gap between scheduled vesting and actual market selling.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a secured token allocation facing a calendar, separated by a line representing the gap between unlocking and selling.

title: Avalanche’s NYSE Rally Exposes the Gap Between Adoption and AVAX Demand
dek: The November 9 surge was real—and leverage expanded with it. The harder question is whether institutional settlement on Avalanche creates lasting value for its native token.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a settlement rail separated from a token-demand endpoint, alongside the title The Avalanche Value-Capture Question.

title: Aptos Unlock Calendars Still List Investors After Vesting Ends
dek: One November calendar projects 14.38 million APT, including investor and insider allocations. Another projects 4.54 million. The original vesting arithmetic explains much of the gap—but the Foundation’s separate 210 million APT staking commitment poses a harder question.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of an Aptos coin, padlock and November 2026 calendar representing questions about token unlock schedules and restrictions

title: Bitcoin at $76,000: The Monday Rebound That Still Needs Proof
dek: Bitcoin stabilized near $76,000 after a sharp selloff, but ETF outflows, a misleadingly calm funding market and a rebound in open interest make one question unavoidable: is the selling finished, or merely paused?
image_alt: Conceptual editorial artwork showing two opposing stone-like market masses compressing a narrow illuminated seam, symbolizing uncertainty between Bitcoin recovery and renewed selling; no market data are depicted.

title: Mercado Bitcoin Said the Hack Was Contained. The Wallets Kept Draining.
dek: The exchange announced rapid containment. Researchers say customer deposit addresses continued transferring funds. The unanswered question is who still controlled the signatures.
image_alt: Editorial illustration contrasting a Mercado Bitcoin containment announcement with later reported transfers from a network of cryptocurrency deposit addresses.

title: While CLARITY Stalls, Regulators Rewrite Crypto’s Rulebook
dek: Before Congress changes hands, SEC exemptions, CFTC proposals, and stablecoin implementation are creating sharply different pathways for digital assets.
image_alt: Editorial artwork showing the U.S. Capitol behind SEC, CFTC, and OCC rulebooks and a January 3 calendar.

title: The freeze came too late. But which delay actually mattered?
dek: The Binance wallet takeover exposed two clocks in stablecoin enforcement: the long interval before anyone proposed a freeze, and the shorter but consequential interval while a proposed restriction awaited execution.
image_alt: Editorial artwork of a secured vault and frozen stablecoin symbols, contrasting the long pre-proposal delay with the shorter freeze-approval window

title: RWA Token Demand vs. the Narrative: What the Largest Holders Actually Show
dek: Tokenized assets are attracting capital, and trading in real-world-asset derivatives is booming. But those milestones tell us remarkably little about who is buying the cryptocurrencies attached to the story.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of an institutional bank, RWA token labels, and an investigative ledger, contrasting financial adoption with unproven crypto-token demand

title: When Risk-Off Is Not a Crisis: What the November Selloff Really Proved
dek: A technology rout, falling oil and a crypto derivatives divergence exposed market fragility. The evidence for a systemic break—or a lasting AI bust—is far thinner.
image_alt: Abstract editorial illustration of opposing financial-market forces converging at a fractured central seam; no market prices are depicted.

title: The Leverage Trap: Crypto's Fragile November Market
dek: Market value was slipping while derivatives exposure expanded. The dangerous part wasn't a certain crash—it was how little the positioning data revealed about who would be forced to move first.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of two heavy opposing structures separated by a narrow illuminated gap, suggesting pressure building around thin market liquidity

title: Monad’s November 24 Unlock Has a $300 Million Question: Who Can Actually Sell?
dek: Conflicting calendars put Monad’s anniversary release near 16.6–17.1 billion MON. The vesting math is clearer than the market’s capacity to absorb it.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a large layered supply compartment beside sparse bid-like marks, illustrating that unlocked tokens are not automatically sold. No market data is depicted.

title: After the Midterms, CLARITY’s Hardest Vote Is Still Ahead
dek: Democrats’ wins reshape the next Congress. They do not turn a stalled crypto market-structure bill into a lame-duck certainty.
image_alt: An editorial illustration of the U.S. Capitol between calendar pages as lawmakers pass legislation across the transition into a new Congress.

title: Bitcoin’s Open-Interest Filter Failed Its Simplest Test
dek: A timestamp correction rescued a plausible derivatives signal from look-ahead bias. It did not show that open interest improves on price momentum.
image_alt: Editorial illustration: separate teal price and rust open-interest paths diverge over a faint conceptual grid beside the words The Open Interest Question; the paths are not market data.

title: Binance's Four-Hour Wallet Takeover: 50 Authorizations, One Malicious Delegation, and a Delayed Revocation
dek: The chain records the takeover and its end to the second. It cannot tell us why the emergency response took nearly four hours.
image_alt: Editorial timeline showing 50 authorization attempts, one delegation, and 3 hours 49 minutes 36 seconds until revocation

title: Crypto’s November Stress Test: Liquidity, Custody and the Limits of Control
dek: From exchange thefts and frozen stablecoins to election-driven legislation and a sanctioned Moscow trading venue, the same question keeps resurfacing: who can actually move the money?
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a Bitcoin coin, fractured lock, U.S. Capitol, and labeled blocks representing ETF flows, legislation, exchange security, DeFi, and sanctions.

title: The Token Unlock Calendar Has a Liquidity Problem
dek: A 90-day wave of scheduled crypto releases looks alarming on paper. But reported float, recipient behavior and buy-side depth determine whether the supply ever reaches the market.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a glowing open lock and crypto tokens beside the words The Supply Behind the Float

title: DeepBook’s Supply Question: Is the Treasury Locked or Discretionary?
dek: A reported 5.27-billion-token holder, conflicting circulation figures, and an unanswered question about who can move DEEP.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a gold vault door with an interrupted lock mechanism, representing uncertainty over DeepBook token custody and transfer restrictions.

title: Bitcoin’s Recovery Has a Ceiling—and the Evidence Is Still Divided
dek: A November 3 market snapshot showed improving short-term momentum beneath stubborn higher-timeframe resistance. The harder question is what would turn a rebound into a genuine reversal.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a rising teal pathway approaching a solid amber overhead barrier, symbolizing a Bitcoin recovery facing resistance; not a market chart.

title: The Uniswap Rebound That Failed the Liquidity Test
dek: A rally can be real and still be a bad trade. That distinction became the defining feature of Uniswap’s UNI token on November 2, when a plausible intraday recovery collided with deteriorating visible liquidity, limited room to the next resistance level, and fresh questions about the source of selling pressure.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of UNI market scrutiny alongside cautionary imagery referencing the reported Binance wallet exploit

title: Bitcoin’s Quiet Lead in a Weak Crypto Market
dek: Ether and Solana fell further, while Bitcoin’s own trend deteriorated. Relative strength, it turns out, is not the same thing as a healthy market.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of three abstract market paths separating, with a restrained gold path above teal and rust paths; not a factual price chart.

title: Bitcoin’s Price Is Not the Whole Market
dek: Ahead of November’s first US trading session, Bitcoin looked comparatively resilient. Beneath the headline price, market breadth, aggressive selling and uneven liquidation exposure told a less comfortable story.
image_alt: Abstract editorial illustration: an illuminated circular opening split by a jagged amber fault line amid layered market-like bands, symbolizing the divide between Bitcoin price and underlying market breadth.

title: The Liquidity Illusion in Crypto’s New Small-Cap Listings
dek: Five token investigations exposed the gap between reported turnover, concentrated ownership and the price at which anyone could actually exit.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of many trading-flow lines narrowing through a small opening, representing the gap between reported crypto volume and usable liquidity.

title: Bitcoin’s $78,000 Rebound Has a Missing Ingredient: Proof of Spot Demand
dek: Leverage has been coming out of the market. ETF money has turned uneven. And the most important question about the bounce remains unanswered: who is actually doing the buying?
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a dark Bitcoin coin suspended above a broken luminous market path, representing an unconfirmed rebound rather than market data.

title: Bitcoin’s Selloff Was Real. The Leverage Story Is More Complicated.
dek: The October 29 decline carried the unmistakable fingerprints of forced long liquidations. But a closer look at funding, order flow and open interest suggests a market that shed leverage during the shock—and then began rebuilding it.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a Bitcoin coin descending steps above tangled red threads, representing leverage risk rather than market data.

title: Six Trades. Three Wallets. One Unsettling Launch.
dek: SolZFoundation arrived with a privacy-bridge story and a tiny Pump.fun market. Its first indexed trades tell a more immediate story: every observed buyer sold exactly what they bought.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of three anonymous wallets linked to a coin and exit doorway, representing a launch investigation rather than an on-chain map.

title: Institutional Crypto Adoption Is Real. Token Demand Is Still on Trial.
dek: Canton Coin and Chainlink are finding their way into serious financial infrastructure. The harder question is whether that progress is creating economic demand for CC and LINK—or simply a better story to trade.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a financial building and an isolated token joined by a fragile bridge, representing the question of token demand.

title: Bitcoin Is Holding Up. The Tape Is Less Convincing.
dek: A resilient Bitcoin, weaker altcoins, and violent pockets of turnover make a deceptively calm crypto market. The deeper story is in the divergence between relative strength and absolute momentum.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a black Bitcoin coin balanced on a narrow support above an uneven surface, representing fragile resilience rather than market data.

title: AERO at $0.68: The Merger Is Real. The Reversal Isn't.
dek: AERO is testing the boundary between an ordinary post-launch shakeout and a deeper repricing. The chart is beginning to stabilize, but the economics tell a more complicated story.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of joined aerodynamic forms and a separate tilted token, representing a merger and an unproven reversal.

title: Bitcoin’s $1.2 Million Buying Imbalance—and the Reversal It Hasn’t Proven
dek: On October 26, the crypto market looked calm on the surface. Beneath that calm, spot buyers and derivatives traders were telling a more complicated story.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a bright current that dissolves before reaching a Bitcoin coin, representing unconfirmed buying pressure rather than market data.

title: WEFT’s First Week: Who Owns the Float, Who Controls the Exit?
dek: Weft Finance has a functioning market, a public tokenomics story and a strikingly concentrated supply. The harder questions are about what the ledger proves—and what it doesn’t.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a token caught in a tightening woven mesh beside a narrow exit, representing constrained float and liquidity questions.

title: VIRTUAL’s Apparent Alpha Has a Much Bigger Risk Story
dek: A short-window momentum model looks surprisingly good. The underlying token is also unusually volatile, heavily exposed to Bitcoin, and far from passing the tests that would make that result trustworthy.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a bright rising arrow breaking through glass while a dark shadow falls below, representing apparent alpha and hidden risk.

title: RUNE’s Quiet Repricing Problem: A Real Network, an Unsettled Token Thesis
dek: THORChain is still moving meaningful value across chains. Its token is a fraction of its former price. The gap is intriguing—but the case for a recovery is more complicated than either number suggests.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a protected network lattice beside a tilted token, representing the gap between network activity and token thesis.

title: PYTH’s Revenue Breakthrough Meets a 2.125 Billion Token Unlock
dek: A real financial-data business is emerging behind PYTH. The harder question is whether its new token-buying mechanism can mature quickly enough to matter before May 2027.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a key opening a vault as blank token discs emerge, representing revenue progress alongside supply unlock risk.

title: Venice AI’s Privacy Promise Has a Verification Problem
dek: The encryption is meaningful. The assurances are not uniform. And even a genuinely private AI product still has to prove why its token should capture the value.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of a frosted privacy screen examined by a narrow beam of light, representing a privacy claim requiring verification.

title: Who Actually Benefits From Crypto Buybacks? EDGE, STONK and the Missing Ledger
dek: EDGE and STONK put two very different revenue stories on the same balance sheet. The harder question is how much economic value survives the journey from customer fees to each circulating token—and what the market has already priced in.
image_alt: Editorial illustration of three hands reaching toward a coin entering an incomplete ledger ring, representing uncertain buyback beneficiaries.
